description.description: What the watch waits for, in plain words (5-10 words). The user reads it on the watch's card, and you in its notice.

sources.description: What to watch. Lines from every source are merged by timestamp. A source with no pods yet is watched until it has some.

namespace.description: The namespace the resource is in

resource.description: The resource as <kind>/<name>: pods/webapp-7f9c, deployments/webapp, statefulsets/db, daemonsets/agent, jobs/backfill, cronjobs/nightly, replicasets/webapp-7f9c

containers.description: Containers to read, by exact name. Omit for the default container, as kubectl logs does; the header names the others.

all_containers.description: Read every container of the pod, as kubectl logs --all-containers does. Not with containers.

previous.description: Read the instance before the last restart instead of the running one, as kubectl logs --previous does. It is finished: nothing arrives on it.

filters.description: Keep only lines from these nodes. Each is a list of values allowed; omit a key for any.

grep.description: A regular expression each line's message must match. Omit to be told of any line.

since.description: Where the watch starts: an RFC 3339 time, its first nanosecond, or an ISO 8601 duration back from now such as PT10M, not after now; its lines count at once. Omit to start now. Not with cursor.

until.description: When the watch ends on time alone: an RFC 3339 time, its last nanosecond, or an ISO 8601 duration from now such as PT2H. At most a day from now, the default.

cursor.description: A next or follow token a read printed, copied whole and exactly: the watch goes on from where that page stopped, with no line repeated or missed, over the token's sources. Not with sources, filters, grep or since.

limit.description: How many matching lines end the watch. Default 1: the first match.

max_bytes.description: How many bytes of matching lines end the watch. Default 16384.

max_message_bytes.description: Cut each message at this many bytes. Default 2048; 0 for the most Kstack keeps of a message, 16 KiB.
